types.name: MCQ — Standard
types.purpose: One question line and four options, exactly one correct. Label options (a)–(d). Distractors must be plausible and similar in length; never use 'all of the above' for Classes 1–8.

types.name: MCQ — Matching
types.purpose: Print two short columns — Column A items (i), (ii), (iii) and Column B items (1), (2), (3) — then four options, each a full pairing sequence such as 'i-2, ii-3, iii-1'. Exactly one sequence is correct.

types.name: MCQ — Fill Up
types.description: Recall in sentence context, with recognition support.
types.purpose: A sentence with exactly one blank written as ________, then four options that could fill it. Label options (a)–(d). Distractors must be plausible and similar in length; never use 'all of the above' for Classes 1–8.

types.name: MCQ — Statement Analysis
types.purpose: Two or three statements numbered I, II, III, then 'Which of the statements given above are correct?' with four options naming combinations (e.g. 'I and III only').

types.name: MCQ — Correct Statement
types.purpose: Ask 'Which of the following statements is correct?' with four independent statements as options; exactly one is true.

answer_schema.example: (b) Sound cannot travel through a vacuum.

types.name: MCQ — Incorrect Statement
types.description: Discriminating true from false claims, inverted.
types.purpose: Four statements as options: three true, one false. The negative word in the stem MUST be written in capitals (NOT, INCORRECT, EXCEPT) so students cannot misread it.

answer_schema.example: (c) They are brittle and break easily.

types.name: MCQ — Identify
types.description: Naming a thing from its properties.
types.purpose: A description or set of clues (a 'Who am I?' riddle works well for Classes 3–6), then four candidate names.

types.name: MCQ — Odd One Out
types.purpose: Four items from one category as options; exactly one does not belong. The answer MUST state the classifying rule, or the item is ambiguous and unmarkable.

answer_schema.example: (c) Potato — it is a vegetable (a stem tuber); the others are fruits.

types.name: MCQ — Data Interpretation
types.purpose: Print a small data table (a header row plus 3–6 rows), then one MCQ answerable only by reading it. The table is part of the question.

types.name: Assertion & Reason
types.description: Logical relationship between a claim and its explanation.
types.purpose: State only the Assertion (A) and the Reason (R). The four standard CBSE directions are added automatically — never restate or paraphrase them.

fixed: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

types.name: MCQ — Multiple Correct
types.description: Complete knowledge of a set, not just one member.
types.purpose: Four or five options, two or more correct. The stem MUST end with '(Select all that apply.)'. The answer lists every correct option letter. Marking is all-or-nothing: full marks only when every correct option and no wrong one is chosen.

types.name: Matrix Match
types.purpose: Column I entries (P), (Q), (R), (S) against Column II entries (1)–(4); an entry may match one or more. Then four options each giving a complete matching such as 'P-2, Q-3, R-4, S-1'. Exactly one option is correct.

types.name: MCQ — Sequencing
types.description: Correct order of a process or events.
types.purpose: Four shuffled steps labelled I–IV, then four options giving orderings such as 'II → IV → I → III'.

types.name: MCQ — Numerical
types.description: Calculation, with options as a check.
types.purpose: A problem, then four numerical options. Every distractor must be the result of a common error (adding instead of multiplying, area instead of perimeter), never a random number.

types.name: MCQ — Case / Passage Based
types.description: Applying a concept to a described situation.
types.purpose: A short scenario paragraph, then a set of 1-mark MCQs drawn only from it, each with four options. The part marks sum to the question's marks.

types.name: MCQ — Analogy
types.purpose: An analogy of the form 'A : B :: C : ?' with four options for the missing term.

types.name: MCQ — Cause and Effect
types.purpose: An event, then four candidate causes or consequences; the student picks the one that follows most directly.

types.name: MCQ — Chronology
types.purpose: Four historical events labelled I–IV, unordered; four options giving chronological sequences.

types.name: MCQ — True/False Combination
types.purpose: Three or four statements labelled I–III, then four options giving True/False patterns for them.

types.name: MCQ — Complete the Series
types.purpose: A number, letter or shape-character series with one missing term, and four options. The answer MUST state the rule.

answer_schema.example: (c) 42 — the differences increase by 2 each time.

types.name: Fill in the Blank
types.purpose: One sentence with exactly one blank written as ________ — never two blanks, or marking becomes ambiguous. The answer lists accepted spellings and plural forms.

types.name: Fill in the Blanks — Word Bank
types.purpose: A box of words printed above, then numbered sentences each with one blank, 1 mark each. The box holds at least one extra word so the last blank is not free.

types.name: True or False
types.purpose: One statement that is unambiguously true or false. Never use 'usually', 'mostly' or 'sometimes'.

types.name: True or False — Correct the False
types.purpose: A statement the student marks True or False and, if false, rewrites correctly. 1 mark for the judgement, 1 for the correction. The answer gives both parts.

answer_schema.example: False — Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system.

types.name: One Word Answer
types.purpose: A definition or clue whose answer is exactly one word or term.

types.name: Match the Following
types.purpose: Two columns; Column A items (i), (ii)… and Column B items (a), (b)… with ONE extra entry in Column B so the last pair is not free. Marks equal the number of pairs.

types.name: Name the Following
types.description: Term recall from definitions, several at once.
types.purpose: Several one-line definitions numbered (i), (ii), (iii) under one instruction, 1 mark each; each answer is a single term.

types.name: Numeric Entry
types.description: Calculation with an exact numeric answer, no options.
types.purpose: A short calculation with a single exact numeric answer and no options. The answer records the unit and any tolerance.

types.name: Classify / Sort
types.purpose: A list of 4–8 items and two or three named groups; the student writes each item under its group.

answer_schema.example: Living — dog, tree, bird · Non-living — car, stone, chair

types.name: Arrange in Order
types.purpose: Four to six shuffled steps, events or numbers; the student writes the correct order (1, 2, 3… in boxes, or ascending/chronological order).

types.name: Odd One Out — with Reason
types.purpose: Four items; the student names the odd one and gives the reason. 1 mark for the item, 1 for the reason.

answer_schema.example: Sulphur — the others are metals; sulphur is a non-metal.

types.name: Full Form / Abbreviation
types.purpose: An abbreviation whose full form the student writes.

types.name: SI Unit / Symbol
types.purpose: A physical quantity; the student writes its SI unit and symbol.

types.name: Tick (✓) or Cross (✗)
types.description: Simple judgement with a non-verbal response.
types.purpose: Short statements numbered (i), (ii), (iii), each followed by an empty box [   ]; the student puts ✓ or ✗. 1 mark each. For children who cannot yet write fluently.

types.name: Very Short Answer
types.description: Single-fact recall or a one-step idea.
types.purpose: A question answerable in about 30 words.

answer_schema.example: The place where a plant or animal lives naturally and gets its food, air, water and shelter.

types.name: Short Answer
types.purpose: A question answerable in 40–60 words. The answer is a marking scheme with one point per mark.

answer_schema.example: (i) It gives light and heat without human effort. (ii) It is the original source of almost all other energy on Earth.

types.name: Long Answer
types.description: Multi-part explanation, often with a diagram.
types.purpose: A question answerable in 100–120 words. The answer MUST be a marking scheme broken into sub-points with their marks, never one flat paragraph.

answer_schema.example: Mouth/saliva 1 · oesophagus 0.5 · stomach/gastric juice 1.5 · small intestine/bile and pancreatic juice 2

types.name: Very Long Answer / Essay Answer
types.description: Sustained argument across a whole topic.
types.purpose: A question needing 150–200 words of sustained argument, e.g. examining a statement with reference to causes, programme and outcome. The answer is a marking scheme.

types.name: Define the Term
types.purpose: Ask the student to define one term in about 25 words. The answer is the near-verbatim definition and its key words.

answer_schema.example: The process by which a liquid changes into vapour below its boiling point.

types.name: Give a Reason
types.description: Causal explanation of a stated fact.
types.purpose: State a fact and ask 'Give a reason'. The answer MUST be a because-explanation, not a description.

answer_schema.example: Wool traps air, which is a poor conductor of heat, so body heat is not lost.

types.name: Differentiate / Distinguish Between
types.purpose: Ask for differences between two things, one point per mark ('any three points'). The answer MUST be paired contrasts — each point states both sides.

answer_schema.example: Composition variable/fixed · properties retained/changed · separation physical/chemical

types.name: Differentiate — Tabular Form
types.description: Contrastive understanding in a required layout.
types.purpose: Ask for differences 'in tabular form'. Print the empty table as part of the question: a header row 'Basis | X | Y' plus one empty row per point.

answer_schema.example: Function: water/food · direction: upward/both ways · cells: dead/living

types.name: Explain the Process
types.purpose: Ask how a process happens, stage by stage, in 80–120 words. The marking scheme is ORDERED: stages must appear in sequence.

answer_schema.example: Evaporation 1 · condensation 1 · cloud formation 1 · precipitation 1 · collection 1

types.name: List / State
types.purpose: 'List any N…' where N matches the marks (½ or 1 mark per item). The answer lists valid items.

types.name: Application / Real-life Scenario
types.description: Transferring a concept to an unfamiliar situation.
types.purpose: A short realistic scenario (two or three sentences, named people, everyday setting) followed by a question that needs the concept to explain or solve it.

answer_schema.example: Microbes multiply faster in warmth 2 · one valid method (boiling, pasteurising) 1

types.name: Justify Your Opinion
types.description: Taking a position and supporting it.
types.purpose: A debatable claim in quotes, then 'Do you agree? Give N arguments to support your view.' The answer is a rubric (position, arguments, evidence), not one right answer.

answer_schema.example: Rubric: clear position 1 · three relevant arguments 2

types.name: Predict the Outcome
types.description: Applying a rule forward to a new case.
types.purpose: 'What would happen if…' about a change to a system, asking for N consequences.

answer_schema.example: Dead matter would pile up 1 · nutrients would not return to the soil 1

types.name: Give Examples
types.purpose: Ask for N examples of one or more categories. The answer rule is 'any valid member of the category', with sample answers.

answer_schema.example: (i) cow, deer (ii) lion, tiger — any valid examples

types.name: Case Study
types.description: Applying concepts to a described situation.
types.purpose: A scenario paragraph of 80–150 words, then exactly three sub-questions (i), (ii), (iii) worth 1 + 1 + 2 marks, each answerable from the scenario plus the chapter. No OR inside a case study.

answer_schema.example: (i) Continuous cropping depletes one nutrient. (ii) Rhizobium in root nodules fixes nitrogen. (iii) Crop rotation — controls pests, improves soil structure.

types.name: Source Based
types.description: Extracting meaning from a historical or documentary source.
types.purpose: A quoted historical or documentary source of 60–120 words (a speech, letter or record), then three sub-questions worth 1 + 1 + 2 marks about who, what and why.

answer_schema.example: (i) Mahatma Gandhi (ii) Truth and non-violence (iii) Mass non-violent movements such as Non-Cooperation and Civil Disobedience

types.name: Unseen Passage / Reading Comprehension
types.purpose: An ORIGINAL passage (250–450 words for Classes 8–10, 120–250 for Classes 3–7) that the student has never seen, then sub-questions of mixed kinds whose marks sum to the question's marks. Never drawn from a textbook and never reused.

types.name: Seen Extract — Prose
types.description: Recall and interpretation of a studied chapter.
types.purpose: Quote a 3–6 line extract from the studied chapter, then three sub-questions (who/what/why and interpretation) worth 1 mark each.

types.name: Seen Extract — Poetry
types.purpose: Quote a 4–6 line stanza from the studied poem, then sub-questions on the poem and poet, a figure of speech, and mood or meaning.

types.name: Data Interpretation
types.purpose: A bar graph, pie chart or line graph supplied as data in `figure` (the paper prints the chart), then sub-questions answerable only by reading it: a direct read, a comparison, and one calculation.

types.name: Picture Based
types.description: Observation and inference from an image.

types.name: Dialogue / Conversation Based
types.description: Comprehension of a spoken exchange; inferring relationship and intent.
types.purpose: An ORIGINAL short conversation of 4–8 lines between named speakers, then sub-questions on why, what and who, 1 mark each.

types.name: News Report / Notice Based
types.description: Extracting facts from a functional text.
types.purpose: An ORIGINAL short notice or news report (school name, heading, date, time, venue, issuer), then factual sub-questions of 1 mark each.

types.name: Experiment / Observation Based
types.purpose: A short observation table from an experiment (substance/condition | observation), then sub-questions that interpret it, with marks per part.

answer_schema.example: (i) B and D — new substances formed. (ii) Carbon dioxide

types.name: Draw a Diagram
types.purpose: Ask the student to draw a neat labelled diagram and label N parts. The student draws — never refer to a figure printed on the paper ('study the given figure'), because there is none. The answer is a marking scheme: diagram, labels, neatness.

types.name: Label the Diagram
types.description: Identifying the parts of a printed figure.

types.name: Ray / Circuit Diagram
types.purpose: Ask the student to draw a ray or circuit diagram for a stated arrangement and state characteristics of the result. The student draws — never refer to a figure printed on the paper ('study the given figure'), because there is none.

types.name: Complete the Flowchart
types.purpose: A flowchart written as text with arrows and blanks, e.g. 'Evaporation → ________ → Precipitation → ________'. 1 mark per blank.

types.name: Complete the Table
types.purpose: A partially filled table (header row plus 3–5 rows) with some cells left blank; 1 mark per blank cell.

types.name: Map Skill
types.description: Locating and labelling on a map.

types.name: Plot a Graph
types.purpose: A small data table printed in the question; the student draws the graph on the graph paper supplied with the answer sheet. Never print or describe a plotted graph.

answer_schema.example: Axes and scale 1 · points plotted 1 · line drawn 1

types.name: Read the Graph
types.purpose: One graph supplied as data in `figure` (the paper prints it), then a single question answerable only by reading values or trends from it.

types.name: Geometric Construction
types.purpose: Give exact measurements and ask the student to construct the figure and write the steps of construction. The student draws — never refer to a figure printed on the paper ('study the given figure'), because there is none.

types.name: Draw and Colour
types.purpose: A one-line instruction to draw a familiar object and colour it as told. The student draws — never refer to a figure printed on the paper ('study the given figure'), because there is none.

types.name: Circle / Tick on the Picture
types.description: Visual discrimination with a non-verbal response.

types.name: Draw the Hands on the Clock
Grammar Item
types.purpose: One self-contained grammar task on one named rule, in an invented sentence.

types.name: Gap Fill — Grammar Passage
types.purpose: An invented short passage with numbered gaps (i), (ii)…, each filled with the correct form of a word given in brackets. 1 mark per gap.

types.name: Error Correction
types.purpose: Sentences numbered (i), (ii)… each containing exactly ONE error; the answer gives the incorrect word and its correction for each. 1 mark each.

types.name: Editing — Omission
types.purpose: Lines of an invented passage each missing one word; the answer gives the word before, the missing word and the word after, for each line.

answer_schema.example: walking / along / the · saw / an / old

types.name: Sentence Transformation
types.purpose: A sentence plus the direction in brackets, e.g. '(Rewrite using so…that)'. The direction is part of the item.

answer_schema.example: He is so weak that he cannot walk.

types.name: Rearrange the Words
types.purpose: The words of one sentence separated by slashes in shuffled order; the student writes the meaningful sentence.

answer_schema.example: Roses are blooming in the garden.

types.name: Reported Speech
types.purpose: One sentence in direct speech; the student reports it.

answer_schema.example: Ravi told Sita that he was going to the market.

types.name: Active / Passive Voice
types.purpose: One sentence and the direction 'Change into passive voice' (or active).

answer_schema.example: The plants are watered by the gardener every morning.

types.name: Connectors / Clause Joining
types.description: Joining sentences with a suitable connector.
types.purpose: Two short sentences to be joined into one using a suitable connector.

answer_schema.example: Although it was raining heavily, we went out for a walk.

types.name: Punctuation & Capitalisation
types.purpose: One unpunctuated, uncapitalised sentence; the student rewrites it correctly.

types.name: Vocabulary Item
types.purpose: One self-contained vocabulary task (word meaning, word use or word choice) in an invented sentence.

types.name: Synonyms & Antonyms
types.purpose: A word; the student writes its synonym or antonym as directed. The answer lists acceptable words.

types.name: Idioms & Phrases
types.purpose: An idiom; the student gives its meaning or uses it in a sentence of their own.

answer_schema.example: Any sentence using it to mean 'very easy'

types.name: Homophones / Confusables
types.purpose: A sentence with two confusable words in brackets; the student chooses the right one.

types.name: Prefix & Suffix / Word Formation
types.purpose: A root word and a direction (add a prefix or suffix); the answer lists valid formations.

types.name: Gender, Number, Tense Forms
types.purpose: A word and the form to write (plural, feminine, past tense).

types.name: Spelling
types.purpose: Four spellings of one word as options; exactly one is correct.

types.name: Letter Writing
types.purpose: A situation naming the writer, class and school and the recipient, and a word limit (100–120 words). The answer is a rubric: format, content, expression.

types.name: Email Writing
types.purpose: A situation calling for an email, with the sender, recipient, purpose and a word limit. The answer is a rubric: format, content, expression.

types.name: Notice Writing
types.description: Notice format: box, heading, date, signature.
types.purpose: A situation naming the issuer (Head Boy, Secretary) and the event, and a word limit (about 50 words). The format is heavily marked. The answer is a rubric: format, content, expression.

types.name: Message Writing
types.purpose: A phone call or situation to be written up as a short message with date, time, to, from and body (about 50 words). The answer is a rubric: format, content, expression.

types.name: Essay / Composition
types.description: Organised extended writing on a topic.
types.purpose: A topic and a word limit (150–200 words for Classes 8–10, less for younger classes). The answer is a rubric: format, content, expression.

types.name: Story Writing
types.purpose: An outline, an opening line or a set of given words, and a word limit. Say which of the three the student is working from. The answer is a rubric: format, content, expression.

types.name: Paragraph Writing
types.purpose: A topic or a few cue words, and a word limit (60–100 words). The answer is a rubric: format, content, expression.

types.name: Analytical Paragraph
types.purpose: Data (a table or described chart) and a word limit (100–120 words); the student describes trends and comparisons. The answer is a rubric: format, content, expression.

types.name: Dialogue Writing
types.purpose: A situation and the two speakers; the student writes a dialogue of 8–10 exchanges. The answer is a rubric: format, content, expression.

types.name: Diary Entry
types.purpose: An event to reflect on, with a word limit (about 100 words). The answer is a rubric: format, content, expression.

types.name: Speech / Debate
types.purpose: A motion or topic, the occasion and a word limit; for a debate, state for or against. The answer is a rubric: format, content, expression.

types.name: Translation
types.purpose: One to five short sentences to translate into the named language.

types.name: Article Writing
types.purpose: A topic, a title requirement and a word limit (120–150 words). The answer is a rubric: format, content, expression.

types.name: Report Writing
types.purpose: An event to report, the reporter's role and a word limit (120–150 words). The answer is a rubric: format, content, expression.

types.name: Numerical / Calculation
types.purpose: A calculation problem with all the data needed. The answer is a marking scheme that gives marks to steps, not only to the final answer.

types.name: Word Problem
types.purpose: A short everyday situation whose difficulty is comprehension, not computation; one clear question at the end. The answer is a marking scheme that gives marks to steps, not only to the final answer.

types.name: Proof / Derivation
types.purpose: A statement to prove or a relation to derive. The answer is a marking scheme listing the steps and their marks.

types.name: Solve the Equation
types.purpose: One equation (or a pair) to solve for the unknown. The answer is a marking scheme that gives marks to steps, not only to the final answer.

types.name: Simplify / Evaluate
types.purpose: One expression to simplify or evaluate, written in LaTeX delimiters \( … \).

types.name: Find the Missing Number
types.purpose: A number sequence, sum or grid with one or two numbers missing, shown as ____.

types.name: Mensuration — Applied
types.purpose: A real object with its dimensions stated in words (never 'the figure shows'), asking for an area, volume or capacity. The answer is a marking scheme that gives marks to steps, not only to the final answer.

types.name: Statistics — Compute
types.purpose: A frequency table printed in the question, and a statistic to compute from it. The answer is a marking scheme that gives marks to steps, not only to the final answer.

types.name: Pattern / Number Series
types.purpose: A number pattern with the next one or two terms to find; the answer states the rule.

types.name: Prove the Identity
types.purpose: An identity to prove, written in LaTeX delimiters. The answer shows the steps from one side to the other.

types.name: Graphical Solution
types.purpose: A pair of linear equations to solve graphically on the graph paper supplied with the answer sheet. Never print or describe a drawn graph.

types.name: Verify / Check
types.purpose: A property and specific numbers to verify it with.

types.name: Estimation & Rounding
types.purpose: A calculation to estimate after rounding to a stated place.

types.name: Maths Case Study
types.description: Mathematics applied to a real-life scenario.
types.purpose: A real-life scenario with its numbers, then sub-questions (i) 1 mark, (ii) 1 mark, (iii) 2 marks. Section E of the CBSE Class 10 paper.

types.name: Experiment Based
types.purpose: Ask the student to describe an experiment: aim, apparatus, procedure and observation. Never refer to a pictured set-up.

types.name: Design an Experiment
types.purpose: A question to investigate; the student designs a simple experiment, naming the control and the variable changed.

answer_schema.example: Destarched plant 1 · cover part of a leaf (variable) 1 · uncovered leaf as control, iodine test 1

types.name: Predict the Code Output
types.purpose: A short program (Python unless stated) in a code block; the student writes its exact output.

types.name: Algorithm Design
types.purpose: A small problem; the student writes numbered algorithm steps.

types.name: Draw a Flowchart
types.description: Representing an algorithm with flowchart symbols.
types.purpose: A small problem; the student draws a flowchart with standard symbols. Never refer to a printed figure.

types.name: Debug the Code
types.description: Finding and fixing errors in code.
types.purpose: A short program with a stated number of errors in a code block; the student identifies and corrects each.

answer_schema.example: Missing colon after range(5); print(i) must be indented.

types.name: Write the Code
types.purpose: A small task; the student writes a program. The answer is a sample program plus a marking scheme.

types.name: Identify Tool / Shortcut
types.purpose: A question about a software tool or keyboard shortcut, with four options.

types.name: Safety / Procedure
types.purpose: Ask for N safety precautions or procedure steps for a stated setting; one mark each.

types.name: Write the Shortcut Key
types.purpose: A task in a named application or the operating system; the student writes its keyboard shortcut, keys joined with +. Use the shortcut the chapter teaches.

types.name: Write the Steps (Software)
types.description: Carrying out a task in an application.
types.purpose: A task in a named application (word processor, spreadsheet, presentation, browser, email); the student writes the numbered steps, giving each menu path as Menu → Option. One mark per key step.

answer_schema.example: Place the cursor 1 · Table → Insert Table 1 · set 3 columns and 4 rows, click Insert 1

types.name: Write the Spreadsheet Formula
types.description: Formulas and functions on a worksheet.
types.purpose: A small worksheet as a table: the header row is the column letters and the first column the row numbers. Parts (i), (ii)… each name a cell and a result; the student writes the formula or function, starting with =, that goes in it. 1 mark each.

types.name: Circle the Correct Answer
types.purpose: One short sentence with two or three choices written inline in brackets and separated by slashes, e.g. '( kitten / puppy / calf )'. Exactly one choice is correct. Do not use an options list.

types.name: Join with a Line
types.purpose: A two-column table: things on the left, their matches on the right in shuffled order, with a dot • after each left item and before each right item. The student draws lines. 1 mark per pair.

answer_schema.example: Cow — Shed · Bird — Nest · Dog — Kennel

types.name: Cross Out the Wrong One
types.purpose: Four or five simple words in one line; exactly one does not belong, and the student crosses it out. The answer names the word and why.

types.name: Complete the Pattern
types.purpose: A repeating pattern of shape characters (▲ ● ■ ★ ◆) or letters/numbers with a blank ____ for the next item. Use characters only — never describe a picture.

types.name: Bigger / Smaller / Compare
types.purpose: Two or three number pairs with a circle ◯ between each; the student writes >, < or = in the circle.

types.name: Find and Circle (Word Search)
types.purpose: A letter grid of 4–6 rows as a table, and 3–5 words to find. Place every word left-to-right inside a single row, then fill the remaining cells with letters. 1 mark per word. The answer gives the row of each word.

answer_schema.example: SUN row 1 · RAIN row 2 · WIND row 3 · CLOUD row 4

types.name: Cut and Paste / Sort into Boxes
Write the Opposite
types.purpose: Two to four simple words each followed by × and a blank; the student writes the opposite.

types.name: Complete the Number Grid
types.purpose: A table of consecutive numbers (two rows of five) with some cells left blank; ½ or 1 mark per blank as the marks allow.

types.name: Rhyming Words
types.purpose: Two to four simple words; the student writes a word that rhymes with each. The answer lists acceptable rhymes.

answer_schema.example: (i) hat, mat, bat (ii) bee, sea, free

types.name: OR Group
types.description: One slot, N alternatives; the student attempts exactly one.

types.name: Choice Pool
types.description: N independent items; the student attempts any K.

types.name: Sub-Question Set
types.description: One parent item with parts whose marks sum to the parent's marks.

types.name: Common Stem Group
types.description: One shared stimulus serving several separately numbered questions.

types.name: Word Bank Group
types.description: A box of words shared by several fill-in-the-blank items.

types.name: VI Alternative
types.description: A text substitute for a figure-dependent question.

types.name: Instruction Block
types.description: General instructions at the head of a paper or section.
